system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Positions Against the Buyer Playbook

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Start 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia Frost's written authority (none given) | Seller is already at our conditional fallback |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | 5x higher |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | 5x higher, and loses first-dollar recovery |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Amelia Frost's written approval; none given) | Shortened without authority |
| Time-limit spillover (12.3/13) | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Would override the title and fundamental regime |
| Title and capacity | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Fundamentally departs from our structure |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out to the maximum extent enforceable | No fraud carve-out |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Sch 7) | Whole data room, accounts, statutory registers and public records | Specific fair disclosure only | Rejects our standard |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; qualifiers only with named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Blanket exclusion |
| Bluefen (3, 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied before Completion | Consent-on-delivery and endeavours standard |
| Riverlark (2, 7) | Release to be provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Post-Completion release with no undertaking |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow) | Not itemised; "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded | Silent exclusion from funds flow |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Too narrow |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6, Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach either way | Materiality assertion without evidence |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Seller conclusion is unsupported |
| Tax and IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open; no unlimited liability assumed | Seller treats them as closed |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register at DD-012 evidences title | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence required; DD-012 is internal | Relies on an internal source |

## 2. Material issues and reasoning

**a) Fundamental/title regime collapsed into the general regime.** This is the most serious issue. Title and capacity warranties are the foundation of a share purchase. Putting them under the 20% cap, the AUD 250,000 basket and the 18-month limit means a title defect on a AUD 24m deal could be capped at AUD 4.8m and time-barred after 18 months. Combined with the "any limitation applies to all Claims" wording, this is a hidden override. Reject outright. Our position is a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.

**b) Fraud carve-out missing.** The exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature." Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the fullest extent enforceable. Our playbook says no one may waive this. The Seller's Disclosure Letter 1.1 (everything in the data room is disclosed) also creates a risk that a deliberately hidden item is argued to be "disclosed." The carve-out should expressly say that disclosure of data-room material does not defeat a fraud or concealment claim.

**c) Disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions together gut our recourse.** Whole-data-room disclosure (1.1), general public-register disclosure (1.2) and the Clause 8.3 knowledge bar mean that anything we could have found counts against us. Reject all three. Require specific disclosure against specific warranties. The knowledge provision, if retained at all, needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**d) Bluefen is material and unresolved.** Bluefen is about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m). The Seller's own disclosure says no final written consent is included and no evidence of satisfied conditions exists. "Reasonable endeavours" and "satisfied on delivery" are not acceptable for a material customer consent. Require effective written consent and evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion, as a condition precedent, not a post-delivery mechanic.

**e) Riverlark creates a funding and security risk.** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding and unpaid. A release "following Completion" leaves the security in place after we have paid for the shares. The fix is a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, per the playbook.

**f) Funds flow silently excludes the bonuses.** The AUD 420,000 in conditional Completion bonuses is not in the draft funds flow, and the Disclosure Letter says on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are unknown. Calling this "a matter for the Seller" does not fix the funds flow. Either itemise the amount plus on-costs as a Completion line item, or make it expressly seller-funded with a specific indemnity. Confirm on-costs estimates before agreeing the figure.

**g) Ironquay IP is under-protected.** The indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions the transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee, and the AUD 180,000 open amount is not independently verified in either direction. Broaden the indemnity to cover all SOW fees, the transfer of Project Materials and related losses, and keep the SOW3 cure mechanism. Ask for payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment before Completion.

**h) Export/privacy incident (DD-006) needs process, not a conclusion.** The Seller's "not expected to be material" is an assertion, not evidence. The disclosure says it is preliminary and does not establish access, scope or notification duty. We should not assume a breach, harm, notification obligation or numeric claim in either direction. Require log preservation, a completed investigation, and regular written updates before Completion. Consider a specific indemnity for notification and remediation costs if the matter becomes reportable. That is a deal-team decision, not a finding.

**i) Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000) need assessment.** The Seller calls them ordinary course. The disclosure says it is unknown whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued, and notes they should be read together for timing and scope. Assess them on that basis. Do not automatically classify them as Debt or deduct them from the price. Ask for the contracts and a warranty on their terms and accrual status.

**j) Tax and IP are not settled.** The Seller's statement that these are "settled under the general regime" is incorrect. Our playbook keeps them open and assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution. Reject the Seller's characterisation and keep tax and IP warranties in their own categories.

**k) Title evidence is inadequate.** DD-012 is an internal share register supplied by the Seller. The Disclosure Letter (item 10) itself says it does not confirm Buyer verification. Require independent evidence: an ASIC company extract, a PPSR search, the share transfer documentation and evidence of Seller authority, plus a title warranty in the separate regime.

**l) Items not covered by the playbook.** The office lease (DD-007) notification point and the Mossvale assignment restriction (DD-009) should be checked for any landlord or Mossvale consent that might be needed on a share sale. The Seller's non-admission (1.4) and reservation (11) are standard, but they should not be read as confirming that no consent, notice or payment is required. Please check these with the responsible solicitor.

**m) Stale disclosure.** The Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Ask for a bring-down of Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, the incident and the bonuses before any signing.

## 3. Recommendations

1. **Reject** the 20% cap, the AUD 25,000 de minimis, the AUD 250,000 excess-only basket, and the 18-month general period. Counter at 25% / AUD 6m, AUD 5,000, AUD 50,000 first-dollar, and 24 months. Do not offer the 20%/18-month fallbacks without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft.
2. **Reject** the title and capacity spillover. Restore a separate 100%, six-year, outside-basket regime.
3. **Insert** a fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, including an express statement that data-room disclosure does not defeat it.
4. **Delete** the whole-data-room and public-register disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7). Require specific fair disclosure.
5. **Delete** the blanket buyer-knowledge bar in 8.3. Replace with named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, carved out for title, capacity, fraud and specific indemnities.
6. **Bluefen:** make effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions a pre-Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.
7. **Riverlark:** require a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective releases at Completion. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
8. **Bonuses:** itemise AUD 420,000 plus confirmed on-costs in the funds flow, or make them seller-funded with a specific indemnity.
9. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to all SOW fees and transfer of Project Materials, keeping the SOW3 cure. Obtain payment evidence or a confirmatory assignment.
10. **DD-006:** require log preservation, investigation and regular written updates. Do not accept "not material" as a conclusion. Consider a specific indemnity for reportable-incident costs.
11. **Sandbar:** assess the three renewals on the contract terms and accrual status. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
12. **Tax and IP:** reject "settled." Keep them open and in their own categories.
13. **Title:** obtain independent ASIC, PPSR and authority evidence. Treat DD-012 as the Seller's internal source only.
14. **Lease and Mossvale:** confirm whether any landlord or Mossvale consent is required.
15. **Bring-down:** request updated disclosures on all open items before signing.

This analysis is based only on the Seller's documents and the playbook. It should be reviewed by the responsible NSW solicitor before it goes to the Seller.
=== END ADVICE ===
